newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas little changed in stagnant trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas little changed in stagnant trade.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices for March were notionally mixed Friday, with some strength in Texas but minor weakness in the East, as mild weather stretched across most of the U.S, sources said.

Louisiana Gulf Coast swing prices were talked about two cents lower in the mid-$1.70s per mmBtu, with the Henry Hub, La., quoted in the high-$1.70s. This would widen the spread to February indices to about $1.10.
"There's just going to be no weather next week, especially in the Northeast. The market's got to move lower, but no one is around today," one Houston-based trader said.
In the Permian basin, March gas prices were talked more than five cents higher in the $1.61-1.66 range.

"The February market has been higher than March all week. Maybe we're seeing some convergence. Besides that I don't know what it could be," one source said, adding the weather outlook was still calling for moderate temperatures.
At Waha, prices were talked in the $1.60s to about $1.70, also up more than five cents. Southern California border prices also gained about five cents to the mid-$1.60s.
In the Midcontinent, March prices were talked slightly lower in the low-to-mid $1.60s, with the last of March trading at Demarcation also done about two cents lower in the high-$1.60s.
In the East, swing prices in the Appalachian region were talked slightly lower in the $1.83-1.87 area on Columbia Gas and in the high-$1.80s to low-$1.90s on CNG.
